title: Hall panel UI and data flow
idea: The elevator frontend is a hall panel whose reducer owns each button's light, so a press is sent once and the light follows server events.
points: The light goes on at once (SENDING); repeat presses do nothing until OFF.
A server-sent status feed pushes ASSIGNED and ARRIVED events to the panel.
The operator dashboard sends each car's `version` and reloads after a 409.
Follow-ups: destination keypads, peak-hour zoning, and many buildings per service.

messages.label: press ▲
messages.note: The light goes on at once: the reducer moves UP from OFF to SENDING.

messages.label: POST hall-calls {5, UP}
messages.note: One request per press. Repeat presses are ignored while the light is on.

messages.label: INSERT … ON CONFLICT
messages.note: The call is stored once; a car is assigned by the scheduling strategy.

messages.label: 201 HC-1, E2
messages.note: SENT stores the call id and shows E2 next to the arrow.

messages.label: new stop for E2
messages.note: The controller picks up the new stop and E2 starts moving.

messages.label: ASSIGNED HC-1 E1 (failover)
messages.note: Only if E2 fails: the API's status feed reports the new car and the label changes.

messages.label: ARRIVED HC-1
messages.note: A car opens its doors at floor 5. The feed says ARRIVED and the light goes off.

code.title: Hall panel reducer
code.caption: Pure screen logic. Run it, then add a SENT event for HC-9 and predict the output.

walk.text: Each button has a light, a call id and a car. Both start OFF.
PRESS works only when OFF; a second press returns the same state.
SENT lights the button with its id; a failure turns it off with a message.
Feed events find the button by call id; unknown ids are ignored.
The demo: a double press, a network failure, a reassignment and an arrival.

code.title: HallPanel component
code.caption: A React component that renders reducer state and calls the API. Not run here.

walk.text: The reducer state lives here; a server-sent feed dispatches status events.
A press checks the light, dispatches PRESS, then calls the API once.
Each button shows its car and reports its pressed state to screen readers.
Errors render in an alert region so screen readers announce them.

pitfalls: Two fast clicks can both see OFF; the server's 200 replay is the backstop.
Do not turn the light off on a 200; the call is still open.
Interview follow-up: one feed per floor at scale needs fan-out through pub-sub.

quiz.q: In the run, what does the UP button show after ASSIGNED HC-1?
quiz.why: The feed reports HC-1 moved to E1. The reducer finds the button holding HC-1 and swaps its car label.

takeaway: One reducer owns the lights; the server dedupes presses and pushes status.

starters: Should the panel use server-sent events or WebSockets?
How would the operator dashboard show live car positions?
